I approach software the way I approach a photograph: get the structure right, remove what doesn't belong, and pay attention to every detail. Clean, functional engineering in Python and MySQL, shaped by the aesthetic discipline of visual media.

Technical projects

Ongoing project

Ongoing

ESP32 Smart Obstacle-Detecting Cane

ESP32, MicroPython, haptic feedback · Expected completion: mid-2027

A multidisciplinary accessibility prototype that gives visually impaired users real-time spatial awareness and obstacle mapping.

Lower sensorNear the cane tip. Detects low obstacles, surface irregularities and drop-offs in the user's path.
Upper sensorAt chest height. Scans for elevated and overhead hazards a standard cane tip would miss.

A vibration motor in the handle turns distance data into tactile alerts, so the user's hearing stays unblocked. MicroPython continuously reads both sensors and triggers the feedback.

Library Management System

Python, MySQL · Completed 2025–2026 (Grade 12)

A robust backend system that automates inventory management and user transactions. It takes book titles and author credentials as input and validates check-out and check-in statuses against a structured MySQL database.

Python (purely software-based) · Completed 2024–2025 (Grade 11)

Events participated

Hands-on Robotics

Gravitas, VIT Vellore

At the Hands-on Robotics event during Gravitas at VIT Vellore, I got a closer look at how robotics concepts translate into practical, working systems. The session gave me an opportunity to engage with the hardware, understand how individual components contribute to a robot's operation, and see the importance of testing, coordination, and problem-solving during a build. It was a valuable chance to learn by doing, explore the connection between electronics and programming, and strengthen my interest in hands-on engineering and embedded technology.

Planned

What I'm aiming for next, building on the projects above.

Projects planned

  • Study planner with spaced revision (2027): builds a revision timetable from a student's syllabus topics so each topic returns just before it's forgotten.
  • Smart parking monitor (2027–2028): ESP32 boards with ultrasonic sensors detect which spots are free and show them on a simple web dashboard.
  • Photo organiser with AI tagging (2028–2029): a Python and MySQL app that sorts a photo library by scene, date and subject.

Patents planned

  • Distance-based haptic patterns for a two-level cane: a vibration code that tells the user which sensor was triggered (low or overhead) and how far away the obstacle is.
  • Cane-and-phone obstacle map sharing: obstacles detected by one user's cane are logged to a shared map, so other users are warned about hazards on the same route.

Both start with a prior-art search before exploring a filing.

Internships planned (3)

AmazonSummer 2028, after second yearBackend software development. I want to see how databases and backend systems run at very large scale, building on my Python and MySQL work.

MetaEarly 2030, final-year semesterSoftware engineering. I want to build for products used by billions of people and bring my visual eye to how they feel to use.
